title: Editing choices in film
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:15Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The closest bank point covers lighting, framing and editing together, and its editing treatment is only a line on quick and slow cuts, so it is broader than this point, which needs the order and length of shots, montage and slow motion.

draft.title: Editing choices in film
card: Shot order
Editors choose which shots come first and which follow. Putting a shot of a worried face before a shot of a stranger makes viewers read the stranger as a threat.
Shot length
A long shot gives viewers time to look and feel. A run of very short shots speeds the pace and can build tension or panic.
Montage
A montage joins many short shots to show time passing or to link ideas. A training montage can show a character improving over weeks in a few seconds.
Slow motion
Slow motion stretches a moment so viewers focus on it. It can make an action look graceful, painful or important.
draft.remember: Editors shape meaning by choosing the order, length and speed of shots.

a.q: A film shows a girl smiling, then a shot of a puppy, then a shot of her smiling again. What does the order of shots suggest?
opts: The puppy is the reason she is happy
The girl is afraid of the puppy
The puppy is unrelated to the girl
Time is passing quickly in the scene
a.why: Placing the puppy between two smiles leads viewers to link the two, so the puppy seems to cause her joy. It is not a montage of time passing, because only one moment is shown.
a.clue: Viewers join shots that sit side by side.

b.q: In a chase scene, a director cuts between shots that each last under a second. What is the most likely effect on viewers?
opts: It makes the scene feel fast and tense
It makes the scene feel calm and peaceful
It lets viewers study each setting closely
It shows that many weeks have passed
b.why: Very short shots speed the pace, which builds tension or panic. The calm and close study described in the other options come from long shots, and time passing is the job of a montage.
b.clue: Think about what quick, short shots do to the pace.

a.best: The puppy is the reason she is happy

b.best: It makes the scene feel fast and tense

problems.detail: 'A long shot gives viewers time to look and feel' misuses a film term. A 'long shot' is a camera framing (a wide shot showing a whole figure or setting), not a shot of long duration. The term for duration is a 'long take' or 'longer shot'. Students learning film language will be misled. Reword, e.g. 'A shot held for a long time (a long take)…'.

Why (b) repeats the same confusion: 'the calm and close study described in the other options come from long shots'. It should say long takes, or shots held for a long time, so it is not mistaken for the framing term 'long shot'.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer. The card and why (b) use 'long shot' to mean a shot of long duration, but in film language a long shot is a wide framing; it should say 'long take' or 'a shot held for a long time'.
